sections.name: File setup, MomentOption
sections.title: Header and choice shape
sections.what: States that these types describe the moment as shown before lock, with no model answers, and defines one choice a fan can pick: a key and a display label.
sections.why: Reason stated in the comment: nothing after the cutoff and no model answer.
sections.watch_out: The key is what gets stored, so renaming a key breaks the meaning of past calls.

sections.name: PrelockMoment
sections.title: What a fan sees before locking
sections.what: Lists everything about a moment a fan can see before locking: teams, venue, target, balls and wickets left, phase, striker, bowler, recent form, leverage, the cutoff time, the question and the choices.
sections.why: Reason stated in the comment: the moment shows only what was known before the cutoff.
sections.watch_out: This type only describes shape; whether a field is safe to show is decided where the moment is built.

sections.name: lockInput, LockInput, LockedCall
sections.title: Lock request and confirmation
sections.what: Defines the lock request (a moment, one choice and a confidence between 50 and 99 percent) with messages shown when it is wrong, and the confirmation with the server's lock time.
sections.why: The comment says the server sets the lock time, not the browser.
sections.watch_out: The confidence limits here must match the limits in the lock rule in the service.

sections.name: CallReview, DECISION_TYPE_LABEL
sections.title: Full review of one graded call
sections.what: Describes what a graded call's review shows: the pick and confidence, grade and calibration, rating before and after, choices with estimates, the reveal, receipts with hashes, the after-lock path and the strongest alternative. Also maps each decision type to a readable label.
sections.why: The comments say the review shows the grade, the rating change, the reveal and the receipts.
sections.watch_out: Only three decision types have labels, so a new type without one shows its raw name.

sections.name: NotebookCall
sections.title: One row in the Notebook
sections.what: Describes one call row in the Notebook: moment, teams, phase, decision type, question, pick and best option, confidence, lock time and grade fields.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond its shape.
sections.watch_out: The row contains the best option, so it should only be shown to the fan who made the call.

sections.name: Notebook
sections.title: Shape of the Notebook page
sections.what: Describes the whole Notebook: sport, active filter, decision types, calls, reliability buckets, Brier series, skill domains, the rating with its history, and warnings.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the page's sections.
sections.watch_out: The rating is shared across filters, so its number may not match the filtered list.

sections.name: ShareCardData
sections.title: What a share card contains
sections.what: Describes the share card: display name, heading (CALLED IT or MY READ), title, confidence, grade text, match line and calibration label. The comment says it has no email, id or pick.
sections.why: The comment says this avoids leaking identifying details and the best option.
sections.watch_out: The type only checks shape; the builder decides what goes into the card.

sections.name: SeasonFile
sections.title: Shape of the printable season summary
sections.what: Describes the season summary: display name, generation time, counts, hit rate, mean Brier and read, best and worst calls, reliability, rating, Alter Ego label and warnings.
sections.why: The comment describes this as a printable summary.
sections.watch_out: Several values can be empty when there are no graded calls, so the page must handle empty values.

summary: Defines the shapes of Decision Lab data as the pages see it: pre-lock moments, the lock request, reviews, the Notebook, share cards and the Season File.
purpose: Gives the Lab's pages and services one agreed description of each data item, so they cannot quietly drift apart.
why: Likely reason: the types separate what fans see before lock from what is revealed after it.
how: 1. Describes a moment before lock. 2. Validates the lock request with rules for the option and the confidence range. 3. Describes a locked call and its review, including the after-lock path and the strongest alternative. 4. Maps decision types to readable labels. 5. Describes Notebook rows, the Notebook, the share card and the Season File.
inputs: No runtime input except the lock request, which the schema validates.
outputs: Type definitions and the lock request schema.
risks: Types are checked only when the code is built. Data arriving from the browser is checked only by the lock request schema. The share card type leaves out the pick on purpose.
debug: If a page shows undefined fields, compare the field with this file and with the service that builds it. If a lock request fails, read the error text, which gives the confidence message.
